title: digital product passport
definition: A Digital Product Passport (DPP) is a standardised digital record that captures and communicates information about a product's material composition, origin, manufacturing process, environmental footprint, repair history, and end-of-life options throughout its lifecycle. Mandated by EU ecodesign and product sustainability legislation, DPPs are designed to be machine-readable and accessible to consumers, regulators, recyclers, and supply chain actors via data carriers such as QR codes or RFID. They are a foundational instrument of circular economy policy and are frequently implemented using blockchain or distributed ledger technology to ensure provenance integrity and tamper-evident audit trails.
